chapter: Early life and the Whitney Bank
title: Born in the French Quarter and moving uptown to Miro and Bolivar streets
summary: Dawson was born downtown on Decatur between Esplanade and Barracks, attended a Catholic school until third grade, then the family moved uptown.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you where you were born. Yeah, Charlene. What, you know what street you were born on?

Uh, down, down in the French course at, uh, on St. Mary, uh, uh, by the, by the, between, uh, uh, Espenade, uh, on Decatur between, uh, uh, Charlize and, uh, I mean, on the trail between Espanade and Barracks.
And how long did you live there?

Well I went to school. I went to Catholic school there. Somewhere there was a Catholic school in that block. I went to school there. It was all white school. I went to school there until I got up to the fourth grade I think it was. Third grade, that's right. Then I left and then my people left from there, from downtown and they moved uptown, Miro Street. My people moved on Miro between Tulane Avenue and Gravy. And my daddy had bought a house on there. We had our own place on Miro between Gravy and Perdida. And then came when we moved after he sold that place. He sold a home and we moved to Bolivar between Gravy and Perdida on Bolivar Street.
See you later. Alright. See you later.
Uh huh. Now that's where we come up from. All my sisters and my brothers were all raised up. Right around Bolivar between Gravy and Perdida.
How old were you when you moved to Miro?
And how old were you when you hit Bolivar?
I was just about the age, you see about uh, say about 13 or 14, something like that there. Yeah. And I raised up from there on, see.
Well how long did you live on Miro Street?
Oh, well I was just about uh, I believe I must have been about 10 or 11 years old when I was on Miro Street then.
